sources.quote: Dr. Bibha Chowdhuri was born on 3 July 1913 in Kolkata, into a progressive zamindar family from Bhandarhati in Dhaniakhali Block in Hooghly district, West Bengal.
She received M.Sc. degree in Physics under Professor D.M. Bose at University of Calcutta in 1936 (i.e. 1934-36 batch).
Following the completion of her M.Sc. degree, Bibha Chowdhury began her professional and research career at the Bose Institute in Kolkata.
She received M.Sc. degree in Physics under Professor D.M. Bose at University of Calcutta in 1936 (i.e. 1934-36 batch).
Among her key collaborators were D. M. Bose and A. K. Ganguly, who worked with her for 5 and 8 years, respectively.
In 1945, Bibha Chowdhury moved to Manchester to work in the laboratory of Sir Patrick Blackett, where she investigated extensive air showers using cloud chambers and Geiger-Müller counters.

Dr. Bibha returned to India in 1949 and became the first female researcher to work at the prestigious TIFR.
Bibha Chowdhury later joined the Physical Research Laboratory (PRL) in Ahmedabad, working under the leadership of Dr. Vikram Sarabhai.
Among her key collaborators were D. M. Bose and A. K. Ganguly, who worked with her for 5 and 8 years, respectively.

In recognition of her contributions to science, the International Astronomical Union named a star "Bibha" in 2019-a white-yellow dwarf located approximately 340 light-years away in the constellation Sextans.
